Question: Define the function \(f_1\) on the positive integers by setting \(f_1(1) = 1\) and if \(n = p_1^{e_1} p_2^{e_2} \cdots p_k^{e_k}\) is the prime factorization of \(n \gt 1,\) then \[ \begin{aligned} &f_1(n) = (p_1 + 1)^{e_1 - 1}(p_2 + 1)^{e_2 - 1} \\ &\quad \cdots (p_k + 1)^{e_k - 1}. \end{aligned} \] For every \(m \ge 2,\) let \(f_m(n) = f_1(f_{m-1}(n)).\) For how many \(N\) in the range \(1 \le N \le 400\) is the sequence \((f_1(N), f_2(N), f_3(N), \ldots)\) unbounded? Note: a sequence of positive numbers is unbounded if for every integer \(B,\) there is a member of the sequence greater than \(B.\)
Solution:
Write \(F=f_1\). Including the starting value \(N\) in the sequence does not affect boundedness, since adding one initial term cannot make a bounded sequence unbounded. The useful quantities to track are the prime exponents, because the definition transforms prime powers directly.

First consider \(n=2^a3^b\), where \(a,b\) are nonnegative integers. For a real number \(t\), write \(t_+=\max(t,0)\). An absent prime contributes nothing, and a prime with exponent \(1\) disappears. Therefore
\[
F(2^a3^b)=2^{2(b-1)_+}3^{(a-1)_+}.
\]
Applying this again gives
\[
F(F(2^a3^b))
=2^{(2a-4)_+}3^{(2b-3)_+}.
\]
Thus every two applications transform the exponents independently by
\[
a\longmapsto\max(2a-4,0),
\qquad b\longmapsto\max(2b-3,0).
\]

If \(a\ge5\), the positive excess \(a-4\) doubles every two steps. In particular, the exponent increases by at least \(1\) each time and becomes arbitrarily large. Likewise, if \(b\ge4\), the positive excess \(b-3\) doubles. Either condition makes the original integer sequence unbounded.

If instead \(a\le4\) and \(b\le3\), the formula for one application of \(F\) shows that the next exponents also satisfy these bounds. Every later integer is therefore at most \(2^4 3^3=432\). We have proved the exact criterion
\[
2^a3^b\text{ has an unbounded sequence}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 a\ge5\text{ or }b\ge4.
\]

Now return to \(N\le400\). If every prime factor at least \(5\) occurs only once, those factors all disappear in the first application. Such an \(N\) therefore has an unbounded sequence exactly when it is divisible by \(32\) or \(81\). There are \(12\) multiples of \(32\) and \(4\) multiples of \(81\) in the range. There is no overlap because \(32\cdot81>400\). None of these multiples can contain a repeated prime at least \(5\), since even \(32\cdot25>400\).

It remains to check repeated primes at least \(5\). Such a prime must be one of \(5,7,11,13,17,19\), because its square is at most \(400\). Two different primes from this list cannot both be repeated, since \(5^2 7^2>400\). The following cases therefore exhaust the remaining possibilities without overlap.

For an exact factor \(5^2\), write \(N=25\cdot2^a3^b s\), where every prime factor of \(s\) occurs once and is different from \(2,3,5\). Since \(2^a3^b s\le16\), we have \(a\le4\), \(b\le2\), and
\[
F(N)=2^{1+2(b-1)_+}3^{1+(a-1)_+}.
\]
The exponent of \(2\) is at most \(3\). The exponent of \(3\) reaches the growth threshold \(4\) only when \(a=4\). The size bound then forces \(N=25\cdot16=400\), which does work: \(F(400)=2\cdot3^4\). If the exact factor is \(5^3\), the remaining multiplier is \(1,2,\) or \(3\), so \(F(N)=36\), which is in the bounded range. Higher powers of \(5\) exceed \(400\).

For an exact factor \(7^2\), the remaining multiplier is at most \(8\), so its exponents satisfy \(a\le3\), \(b\le1\). Consequently
\[
F(N)=2^3 3^{(a-1)_+},
\]
which is in the bounded range. An exact factor \(7^3\) is possible only for \(N=343\). Here \(F(343)=8^2=2^6\), so the sequence is unbounded.

For each of \(p=11,13,17,19\), the only possible repeated exponent is \(2\), and the remaining multiplier is at most \(3\). That multiplier has no repeated prime factor, so \(F(N)=p+1\). These four starting outputs are bounded, as the complete chains show:
\[
12\to3\to1,\qquad 14\to1,
\]
\[
18\to4\to3\to1,\qquad 20\to3\to1.
\]
After reaching \(1\), the sequence stays there.

The only extra values are therefore \(400\) and \(343\). The total is
\[
12+4+2=\boxed{18},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
